text:
Darren Raddysh came home to Toronto on a big contract, and the first month has turned into a referendum on it. The New York Times asked whether he's living up to the deal, and after his penalty preceded Utah's power-play winner on Nov. 3, he took the blame himself; The Hockey News headline had him calling it a "Dumb" penalty. He scored 22 goals for Tampa Bay last season. He has none in 17 games as a Leaf.

The goals are the noisy part. He's playing 23 and a half minutes a night with nine assists, seven on the power play, and the Leafs are a little better in expected-goal share with him on at five on five than without. His own shots add up to only 1.7 expected goals, so this is fewer looks as much as a finishing slump. Last season Evolving-Hockey ranked him 15th among defensemen, with a note that strong teammates flattered him, which is exactly the question Toronto is testing now. Our projection's middle case is 14 more goals, and a few of those would quiet a lot of this.
headline: A big contract, and no goals yet
